messages:
Mara G.: Quick heads up — I'm seeing a steady KV frame growth on Dedicated when running the long-context reranker. Hosted and Private don't exhibit this. Anyone else?

Josh L.: I noticed a canary with similar behavior. Dedicated node RSS climbs ~15% over ~2h. Repro steps?

Mara G.: Repro snippet: run reranker_longctx, ctx=48k, batch_size=1, batching_window=40ms, kvcache.max_frames=22000. After ~90min frame_count and RSS both ramp.

Neha P.: Do we have jemalloc and nvml stats? Host-pinned pages + many arenas can prevent compaction.

Mara G.: From the Dedicated canary: jemalloc.arenas=unbounded, tcache.enabled, nvml.hostpin_pages=12480, rss from 30G -> 36G over 90m. Perf top: runtime::kv_backfill_small_alloc and nvmlHostAlloc at top.

Sana R.: Fleet differences? kernel/driver/THP/cgroups? Those change MADV and reclaim semantics.

Mara G.: Dedicated: kernel=5.15.x, nvidia-driver=470.x, THP=madvise, cgroup=v1, vm.swappiness=10. Hosted: kernel=6.1.x, driver=525.x, THP=never, cgroup=v2, swappiness=60. Private mixed.

Neha P.: MADV_FREE semantics on 5.15 can be lazy; combined with aggressive hostpinning we can see apparent memory growth. What are runtime knobs?

Mara G.: Dedicated had batch_window=50ms (changed last month), kvcache.hostpin_threshold=0.2, kvcache.coalesce=false, backfill_batch=512. Hosted kept batch_window=20ms, hostpin_threshold=0.9, coalesce=true.

Josh L.: That explains it: larger batching_window increases in-flight working set; low hostpin threshold pins many ephemeral frames. Older kernel + MADV_FREE = delayed reclaim.

Mara G.: Quick canary plan: set hostpin_threshold=0.9, batch_window=20ms, backfill_batch=128, enable coalesce, cap jemalloc arenas=8, and change eviction_madvise to MADV_DONTNEED on kernels <6.0.

bench-bot: queued perf test -> reranker_kv_madvise_canary @ 1830002200

Mara G.: Ran canary 2h: RSS ramp reduced ~70%, nvml.hostpin_pages -50%, fragmentation index dropped from 0.42 -> 0.18, kv.reuse improved from 0.62 -> 0.83.

Neha P.: Nice. Next actions: normalize jemalloc arenas in base images, add hostpin_threshold override to infra config, and add metric kv.page_alloc_rate vs kv.page_free_rate to alert when alloc>free for 30m.

Sana R.: Add rollout gating: if kernel <5.18 OR driver <510.x, enable DONTNEED+munmap fallback and avoid MADV_FREE. Also add a check for THP settings and cgroup mode in the deployment playbook.

Josh L.: Also audit who bumped batching_window in Dedicated autoscaler last month — that change correlates with the start of these regressions. If throughput was the reason we'll need a measured rollback strategy.

Raul (infra-bot): noted: autoscaler change 2026-02-18 by ops@infra increased batching_window in pool-west to 50ms. Logging config patch infra-config#389.

Mara G.: I'll open PRs: infra-config to set hostpin_threshold and jemalloc caps, and runtime change to add MADV fallback + a small coalescer that merges adjacent freed frames before munmap.

Josh L.: For longer-term: expose kvcache.hostpin_probability_histogram and implement a hostpin-aware eviction policy so we don't pin low-reuse frames. Also consider a background compaction job for kernels without aggressive reclaim.

Mara G.: Agreed. Short-term rollback + MADV switch + jemalloc cap seems low-risk. We'll roll to affected dedicated pools gradually and monitor kv.delta_alloc_free, nvml.hostpin_pages, and per-token latency.

bench-bot: canary passed 6h. Ready for staged rollout.

Mara G.: Filing a short incident log with timeline, PR links, and the triage/playbook steps. Thanks all :thumbsup:
